title: TAK-003 dengue vaccine protects adolescents during São Paulo’s 2024–2025 outbreak - Bioengineer.org

analysis.time: The study was conducted during the 2024–2025 dengue outbreak in São Paulo, with the publication date of the findings being 2026-09-04. The analysis included data from adolescents over a one-year period.
analysis.location_and_population: The study took place in São Paulo State, Brazil, focusing on adolescents aged 10 to 15 years. The population included 384,546 individuals, with 166,390 participating in the analysis.
analysis.event: A real-world evaluation of the TAK-003 dengue vaccine was conducted, revealing that a single dose still prevents about 60% of symptomatic dengue cases and 75% of hospitalizations one year post-vaccination. The study was reported by researchers from the Federal University of Mato Grosso do Sul, the University of Florida, and Yale School of Public Health.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The study found that the vaccine effectiveness against symptomatic dengue was 59.2% for one dose and 73.1% for two doses. Against hospitalization, effectiveness was 74.6% for one dose and 87.9% for two doses. The study also noted that the dominant viral serotypes shifted during the outbreak, with DENV-3 re-emerging and DENV-4 detected in early 2025.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study was conducted using Brazil’s compulsory dengue surveillance system (SINAN-Dengue) and São Paulo State’s vaccination registry. The findings were published in eClinicalMedicine, and the researchers acknowledged limitations, including the lack of baseline serostatus and potential underreporting of mild infections. The study’s results are considered preliminary and require further long-term surveillance.

analysis.brief_en: A study published in eClinicalMedicine evaluated the TAK-003 dengue vaccine's effectiveness during the 2024–2025 outbreak in São Paulo State, Brazil. The research, conducted by teams from the Federal University of Mato Grosso do Sul, the University of Florida, and Yale School of Public Health, analyzed data from over 166,000 dengue tests among adolescents aged 10 to 15 years. The findings showed that a single dose of the Qdenga vaccine prevented about 60% of symptomatic dengue cases and 75% of hospitalizations one year post-vaccination, while the two-dose schedule provided even stronger protection. The study also noted that the dominant viral serotypes shifted during the outbreak, with DENV-3 re-emerging and DENV-4 detected in early 2025. Despite the vaccine's effectiveness, the researchers emphasized the need for long-term surveillance due to potential risks and limitations, such as the lack of baseline serostatus and the possibility of underreporting mild infections. The results suggest that the vaccine's protection does not wane over time, offering a promising outlook for dengue control strategies.

title: WHO has zeroed in on 6 candidates for a dengue drug, but only 1 in late-stage trials - ThePrint

analysis.time: The report was published on September 8, 2026. The WHO analysis was published this month, and the Phase 3 trial for VIS513 is scheduled to begin in the first quarter of 2027.

analysis.event: The World Health Organization (WHO) has identified six dengue drug candidates with evidence warranting further development, with only VIS513 reaching Phase 3 trials. The analysis was published in The Lancet Microbe, and the WHO highlighted the absence of safe and effective dengue-specific treatments as a gap in the product landscape for care.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The WHO reported over 5 million cases and more than 5,000 deaths in 2023 across 80+ countries. About 80 percent of these cases were in the Americas. analysis.brief_en: The World Health Organization (WHO) has identified six dengue drug candidates with evidence supporting further development, though only one, VIS513, has reached Phase 3 trials.
